tools.name: register
tools.description: Register this agent session with the swarm. Call this first before using other tools.

directory.description: The project directory this instance is working in

label.description: Optional friendly label for this instance

scope.description: Optional shared swarm scope. Defaults to the detected git root.

file_root.description: Optional canonical base directory for resolving relative file paths. Useful when multiple worktrees should share one logical file tree.

adopt_instance_id.description: Optional existing leased instance ID to adopt instead of creating a fresh registration.

tools.name: list_instances
tools.description: List all currently active agent sessions in this swarm scope.

label_contains.description: Filter instances whose label contains this substring (e.g. 'role:implementer')

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Get this instance's swarm ID and registration info.

tools.name: bootstrap
tools.description: Atomic 'where am I?' for swarm state. Returns this instance, peers (excluding self), unread messages, and the task snapshot in one call. Use this on session start, after compaction, or any time you need to rejoin and rehydrate. By default consumes unread messages (mark-as-read); pass mark_read=false to peek.

mark_read.description: When true (default), unread messages are returned and marked read (matches poll_messages). When false, messages are peeked and remain unread.

adopt_instance_id.description: Optional existing leased instance ID to adopt before returning the bootstrap snapshot.

include_terminal.description: When true, include full terminal task rows. Default false keeps bootstrap compact and returns terminal_counts only.

terminal_limit.description: Maximum terminal rows per status to include when include_terminal=false. Default 0 returns counts only.

tools.name: remove_instance
tools.description: Forcefully remove another instance from the swarm. Releases its tasks and locks.

tools.name: deregister
tools.description: Remove this instance from the swarm and clean up its tasks and locks.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to a specific instance by ID.

recipient.description: The instance ID to send the message to

tools.name: prompt_peer
tools.description: Send a durable swarm message to another instance, then best-effort wake its published workspace handle when supported. By default, busy handles are not interrupted; use force only for urgent or corrective updates.

nudge.description: Whether to wake the target workspace handle

force.description: Wake even when the target workspace handle is working; reserve for urgent or corrective updates

tools.name: peek_peer
tools.description: Read recent or visible terminal text from another instance's published workspace handle when supported. This does not send a message or wake the peer.

lines.description: Maximum lines to read from recent sources

tools.name: resolve_workspace_handle
tools.description: Resolve a transport-local workspace handle to the matching swarm instance by validating published workspace identity mappings.

backend.description: Workspace backend name. The current bundled backend is herdr.

handle_kind.description: Type of workspace handle, such as pane

handle.description: Transport-local workspace handle from the backend

validate.description: Validate published identities through the backend and repair stale aliases

tools.name: broadcast
tools.description: Send a message to all other active instances in this swarm scope.

tools.name: poll_messages
tools.description: Check for new incoming messages. Returns unread messages and marks them as read.

tools.name: request_task
tools.description: Create a task for another instance, or leave it open for any instance in this scope.

description.description: Detailed description of what needs to be done

assignee.description: Specific instance ID to assign to, or omit for any taker

priority.description: Priority level. Higher = more urgent. Default 0. Agents claim highest-priority open tasks first.

depends_on.description: Task IDs this task depends on. Task stays blocked until all dependencies reach done.

idempotency_key.description: Unique key to prevent duplicate task creation. If a task with this key exists, returns the existing task.

parent_task_id.description: Optional parent task ID for tree-structured work tracking.

review_of_task_id.description: Optional task ID this review task is reviewing.

fixes_task_id.description: Optional task ID this fix task addresses.

approval_required.description: If true, task starts in approval_required status and must be approved before work begins.

tracker_required.description: If true, complete_task must include tracker_update or tracker_update_skipped.

tracker_provider.description: Optional configured tracker provider name, such as linear, jira, or github_issues.

tools.name: request_task_batch
tools.description: Create multiple tasks atomically in a single transaction. Supports $N references (1-indexed) for dependencies, parent links, review links, and fix links in the batch. Rolls back entirely on validation failure.

description.description: Detailed description of what needs to be done

assignee.description: Specific instance ID to assign to, or omit for any taker

priority.description: Priority level. Higher = more urgent. Default 0. Agents claim highest-priority open tasks first.

depends_on.description: Task IDs this task depends on. Task stays blocked until all dependencies reach done.

idempotency_key.description: Unique key to prevent duplicate task creation. If a task with this key exists, returns the existing task.

parent_task_id.description: Optional parent task ID for tree-structured work tracking.

review_of_task_id.description: Optional task ID this review task is reviewing.

fixes_task_id.description: Optional task ID this fix task addresses.

approval_required.description: If true, task starts in approval_required status and must be approved before work begins.

tracker_required.description: If true, complete_task must include tracker_update or tracker_update_skipped.

tracker_provider.description: Optional configured tracker provider name, such as linear, jira, or github_issues.

tasks.description: Array of task specifications. $N references are 1-indexed positional refs within this array.

tools.name: dispatch
tools.description: Gateway-only: create/reuse a task, wake a live worker, or spawn a worker through the configured spawner.

title.description: Short title for the task to dispatch

message.description: Instructions sent to the worker; defaults to title

role.description: Worker role token without the role: prefix

spawn.description: When false, create/wake only; do not spawn a worker

force_spawn.description: Skip live-worker matching and go straight to the spawn path. Use when you explicitly want a fresh worker pane even if a generalist or matching peer exists.

cwd.description: Spawn cwd; defaults to this instance directory

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for worker spawn/adoption; defaults depend on spawner

workspace.description: Workspace placement policy: "reuse_scope" (default), "new", "current", or backend-specific workspace id

tab.description: Tab placement policy: "reuse_group" (default), "new", "current", or backend-specific tab id

group.description: Logical layout group used for tab reuse, such as a batch or role name

parent_pane_id.description: Explicit parent pane to split from; overrides scope layout reuse

max_panes_per_tab.description: Maximum panes per reused tab before creating another tab

layout.description: Backend-agnostic visual layout intent, such as {"kind":"grid","rows":2,"cols":3} or {"kind":"balance"}

placement.description: Optional workspace placement intent for spawner backends

completion_wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the dispatched task to reach done, failed, or cancelled. Omit or pass 0 to return immediately after handoff/spawn.

force.description: Wake even when target workspace handle is busy

promote.description: VUH-36 per-dispatch promotion override. true=force-promote to the configured work tracker, false=suppress. Omit to let the policy in docs/linear-promotion-policy.md decide.

promote_identifier.description: Explicit tracker identifier (e.g. VUH-31) the operator wants to link to. Forces a `link` promotion decision.

tools.name: claim_task
tools.description: Start work on a task: assigns it to you (if open) and transitions to in_progress in one call. Works on open+unassigned tasks and on tasks pre-assigned to you (status=claimed). Use claim_next_task when you want the server to pick the highest-priority compatible task atomically.

ignore_unread_messages.description: Set true only when intentionally claiming despite unread messages. Default false blocks claiming until poll_messages is called.

tools.name: claim_next_task
tools.description: Atomically claim the highest-priority compatible task. Prefers tasks pre-assigned to you, then open unassigned tasks. Optional filters let specialists claim only matching task types or files.

types.description: Optional task types to consider, such as ['implement'] or ['review']

files.description: Optional resolved file paths to match against task files. A task matches when any listed file overlaps.

ignore_unread_messages.description: Set true only when intentionally claiming despite unread messages. Default false blocks claiming until poll_messages is called.

tools.name: update_task
tools.description: Move a task to a terminal status (done, failed, cancelled). Auto-releases this instance's locks on the task's files. Prefer complete_task when you can provide structured handoff details.

result.description: Result or summary of work done

tools.name: complete_task
tools.description: Complete a claimed task with structured handoff details. Stores the task result as JSON with summary, files_changed, tests, tracker_update/tracker_update_skipped, and followups, then auto-releases locks on the task's files.

summary.description: Concise summary of what changed or what happened

files_changed.description: Files changed or materially inspected for this task

command.description: Command that was run, such as 'bun test'

tests.description: Verification commands or checks and their outcomes

tracker_update.description: Durable work-tracker update details when you updated the configured tracker directly

tracker_update_skipped.description: Exact reason the configured tracker was not updated, plus enough context for a tracker-capable planner/gateway to do it

followups.description: Follow-up work, risks, or reviewer notes

tools.name: report_progress
tools.description: Report first-class progress on an in-progress task so peers can see status without interrupting. Use for multi-minute work; skip for short tasks.

blocked_reason.description: Why progress is blocked. Pass null to clear an earlier blocked reason.

expected_next_update_at.description: Unix timestamp in seconds for the next expected progress update. Pass null to clear.

tools.name: approve_task
tools.description: Approve a task in approval_required status. Transitions to open/claimed (or blocked if deps unmet).

tools.name: get_task
tools.description: Get full details of a specific task in this swarm scope.

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.description: List tasks in this swarm scope, optionally filtered by status, assignee, or requester.

tools.name: get_file_lock
tools.description: Read active lock state for a file without acquiring an edit lock. Use this for review, planning, or conflict inspection when you are not about to edit the file.

tools.name: lock_file
tools.description: Acquire an edit lock on a file. Returns the new lock id on success or the active lock owner on conflict. Normal edit locks held by this instance are auto-released when their task reaches a terminal state via update_task or complete_task. Pass task_id to associate the lock with a specific task — terminal release will then pick it up by task_id regardless of whether the file appears in the task's declared files list (use this when editing files outside the original task.files set). Pass exclusive=true to require that no lock exists on the file (including one held by this same instance) — useful for one-shot operations like spawn mutexes where same-instance re-entry is itself a conflict.

task_id.description: Optional task ID to associate this lock with. When the named task reaches a terminal status via update_task or complete_task, locks tagged with this task_id are released regardless of whether the file is in task.files.

exclusive.description: If true, conflict on ANY existing lock for the file — including one held by this same instance. Default false keeps re-entrant semantics.

tools.name: unlock_file
tools.description: Release a file lock early. Locks are auto-released on terminal update_task or complete_task, so call this only when you finish a file before the task as a whole.

tools.name: kv_get
tools.description: Get a value from the shared key-value store for this scope.

tools.name: kv_set
tools.description: Set a value in the shared key-value store for this scope.

value.description: The value to store (use JSON for complex data)

tools.name: kv_append
tools.description: Atomically append a value to a JSON array in the KV store. Creates the key with [value] if it doesn't exist. If the existing value is not an array, wraps it in one first.

value.description: The value to append (must be valid JSON)

tools.name: kv_delete
tools.description: Delete a key from the shared key-value store for this scope.

tools.name: kv_list
tools.description: List keys in the shared key-value store for this scope, optionally filtered by prefix.

prefix.description: Optional key prefix to filter by

tools.name: swarm_status
tools.description: Return a compact coordination health summary for this instance: peers, unread messages, assigned and claimable tasks, locks, collision/compliance warnings, planner ownership, and a suggested next action.

tools.name: wait_for_activity
tools.description: Block until new swarm activity arrives (messages, task changes, KV changes, or instance changes), then return what changed. Use this only while you own active monitoring responsibility, not as a generic idle loop. Returns immediately if there is already unread activity. Note: returned messages are marked read.

timeout_seconds.description: Max seconds to wait before returning (even if nothing changed). Default 0 means wait indefinitely.
